description: 200 questions on Python lists basics (creation, indexing, slicing, methods, operations; beginner to intermediate)

questions.question: How do you create a list containing the integers 1, 2, and 3?
How do you create an empty list?
Can a list contain elements of different types?
Can a list contain another list?
questions.answer: Yes, this is called a nested list

questions.question: What is a nested list? Give an example.
Are lists ordered?
questions.answer: Yes, elements keep the order in which they were inserted

questions.question: Are lists mutable in Python?
questions.answer: Yes, you can add, remove, or change elements

questions.question: Can a list contain duplicate values?
What does {} create?
questions.answer: An empty dict, not a list. Use [] or list() for an empty list.

questions.question: What does the list() function do?
questions.answer: Creates a list from an iterable (string, tuple, range, dict keys, etc.)

questions.question: What is the difference between a list and a tuple?
questions.answer: A list is mutable; a tuple is immutable

questions.question: What does list({1, 2, 2, 3}) return?
questions.answer: A list of the set's elements, e.g., [1, 2, 3] (order not guaranteed, duplicates removed)

questions.question: What does range(3) produce by itself?
questions.answer: A range object; wrap it with list() to get [0, 1, 2]

questions.question: How do you access the first element of [10, 20, 30]?
How do you access the third element of a list?
How do you access the last element of a list?
What happens if you access an index that is out of range?
What is the index of the last element of a list of length n?
What happens when you access a[0] on a = []?
questions.answer: IndexError: list index out of range (empty list has no element 0)

questions.question: How do you get the second-to-last element of a list?
Can you use a negative index beyond the list length?
questions.answer: No, list[-5] on a 3-element list raises IndexError

questions.question: What does ["a", "b", "c"][-3] return?
questions.answer: "a" (the first element, reached from the end)

questions.question: What type of value does lst[i] return?
questions.answer: The element stored at that index, of whatever type it is

questions.question: Is the end index in a slice included?
questions.answer: No, slices go up to but do not include the end index

questions.question: What is returned by a slice when the start index is beyond the end?
What does [1, 2, 3][5:10] return?
questions.answer: [] (out-of-range slice start returns an empty list, not an error)

questions.question: Does slicing a list create a new list?
questions.answer: Yes, slices always return a new list

questions.question: What does nums[::] produce?
questions.answer: A (shallow) copy of the whole list

questions.question: What does [1, 2, 3, 4][1:1] return?
questions.answer: [] (start equals end gives an empty slice)

questions.question: What is the default value of the start in a slice?
What is the default value of the step in a slice?
How do you copy a list without affecting the original on change?
Does sorted([3, 1, 2]) modify the original list?
questions.answer: No, it returns a new sorted list; the original is unchanged

questions.question: How do you sort a list in descending order with sorted()?
What happens if you call min() on a list with mixed types like [1, "a"]?
questions.answer: A TypeError because int and str cannot be compared

questions.question: What is the difference between list.sort() and sorted(list)?
questions.answer: sort() sorts in place and returns None; sorted() returns a new list

questions.question: What does any([False, True, False]) return?
questions.answer: True (True if at least one element is truthy)

questions.question: What does all([True, True]) return?
questions.answer: True (True if every element is truthy)

questions.question: What does [1, 2, 3].append(4) do?
questions.answer: Adds 4 to the end in place; the list becomes [1, 2, 3, 4]

questions.question: What does append() return?
questions.answer: None (it modifies the list in place)

questions.question: What does [1, 2].extend([3, 4]) do?
questions.answer: Adds each element of [3, 4]; list becomes [1, 2, 3, 4]

questions.question: What is the difference between append([3, 4]) and extend([3, 4])?
questions.answer: append adds the list as ONE element ([1,2,[3,4]]); extend adds its items ([1,2,3,4])

questions.question: What does [1, 3].insert(1, 2) do?
questions.answer: Inserts 2 at index 1; the list becomes [1, 2, 3]

questions.question: How do you add an element to the very beginning of a list?
What happens if you insert at an index larger than the list length?
questions.answer: The element is appended at the end

questions.question: What does [1, 2, 3].remove(2) do?
questions.answer: Removes the first occurrence of 2; list becomes [1, 3]

questions.question: What happens if remove() can't find the value?
If a value appears multiple times, which one does remove() delete?
What does nums = [1, 2, 3]; print(nums.pop()) output?
questions.answer: 3; the list becomes [1, 2] (pop removes and returns the last item)

questions.question: What does [10, 20, 30].pop(1) do?
questions.answer: Removes and returns index 1 (20); list becomes [10, 30]

questions.question: What happens if you call pop() on an empty list?
What does del lst[1] do?
questions.answer: Deletes the element at index 1 in place

questions.question: What does del lst[0:2] do?
questions.answer: Deletes the slice of elements from index 0 to 2 (exclusive)

questions.question: What does [1, 2].clear() do?
questions.answer: Removes all elements; the list becomes []

questions.question: What is the difference between clear() and del lst?
questions.answer: clear() empties the list but keeps the variable; del lst removes the variable entirely

questions.question: What happens if index() can't find the value?
What is the difference between remove() and pop()?
questions.answer: remove() deletes by value; pop() deletes by index and returns the value

questions.question: What does lst = [3, 1, 2]; lst.sort(); print(lst) output?
What does print([3, 1, 2].sort()) output?
questions.answer: None (sort modifies in place and returns None)

questions.question: How do you sort in descending order in place?
What does [3, 1, 2].reverse() do?
questions.answer: Reverses the list in place to [2, 1, 3]

questions.question: What does reversed() return?
questions.answer: A reverse iterator, not a list (wrap with list() to get a list)

questions.question: What does lst.copy() do?
questions.answer: Returns a shallow copy of the list

questions.question: What does b = a do (both lists)?
questions.answer: b becomes another reference to the SAME list; changing one changes the other

questions.question: How do you sort strings by length?
If lst2 = lst1.copy() and you append to lst2, does lst1 change?
questions.answer: No, because copy() creates a separate list

questions.question: If lst2 = lst1 and you append to lst2, does lst1 change?
questions.answer: Yes, both names refer to the same list object

questions.question: What happens if you call sort() on a list with mixed types?
How do you change the element at index 0 to 99?
What happens if you assign to an index that doesn't exist?
questions.answer: IndexError: list assignment index out of range

questions.question: What does lst[1:3] = [100, 200] do?
questions.answer: Replaces the elements at indices 1 and 2 with 100 and 200

questions.question: Can slice assignment change the length of a list?
questions.answer: Yes, replacing a slice with a different-length list shrinks or grows the list

questions.question: What is the difference between lst += [4] and lst = lst + [4]?
questions.answer: += extends in place; lst = lst + [4] reassigns to a brand-new list

questions.question: Do == and is mean the same thing for lists?
questions.answer: No, == checks value equality; is checks whether they are the same object

questions.question: What does a, b = [1, 2] do?
questions.answer: Unpacks the list: a = 1 and b = 2

questions.question: What is extended unpacking?
questions.answer: Using * to capture multiple elements, e.g., first, *rest = lst

questions.question: How do you convert a string to a list of characters?
How do you join a list of strings into one string?
Can a list be used as a dictionary key?
questions.answer: No, lists are unhashable (mutable); use a tuple instead

questions.question: How do you check if a list is empty?
How do you check if a list is NOT empty?
What does bool([0]) return?
questions.answer: True (the list contains an element, regardless of its value)

questions.question: How do you iterate over all elements of a list?
How do you get both index and element in a loop?
What does enumerate(["a", "b"]) produce when looped?
How do you start enumerate at 1?
What does zip([1, 2], ["a", "b"]) produce when looped?
How do you loop over a list using indices?
questions.answer: for i in range(len(lst)): then lst[i]

questions.question: How do you iterate a list in reverse order?
What happens if you append to a list while looping over it?
questions.answer: It can cause an infinite loop because the list keeps growing

questions.question: How do you sum all elements of a list with a loop?
How do you find the largest element without max()?
How do you loop over a matrix (list of lists)?
questions.answer:
for row in matrix:
    for item in row:

questions.question: How do you get every other element of a list?
How do you get a reversed copy without changing the original?
How do you get the middle element of [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]?
How do you flatten a list of pairs like [[1, 2], [3, 4]]?
questions.answer: Use a nested comprehension: [x for row in matrix for x in row]

questions.question: What does [[0] * 3 for _ in range(3)] create?
Why is [[0] * 3] * 3 a bad way to build a matrix?
questions.answer: All rows refer to the SAME inner list; changing one row changes them all

questions.question: What is the difference between == and is on two equal lists?
questions.answer: a == b is True if values match; a is b is False if they are different objects

questions.question: What does min([[1, 2], [0, 9]]) return?
questions.answer: [0, 9] (lists compare element-wise, so the smaller first element wins)

questions.question: How do you check whether a value occurs in a list?
How do you create a list of the keys of a dictionary?
How do you create a list of the values of a dictionary?
Does reverse() return a new list?
questions.answer: No, it reverses in place and returns None

questions.question: What is a 'list literal'?
questions.answer: A list written directly with square brackets, e.g., [1, 2, 3]

questions.question: How do you get the number of elements in a list?
What does len([1, [2, 3]]) return?
questions.answer: 2 (the nested list counts as one element)

questions.question: What does samp = [1, 2, 3]; samp[1] = 99; print(samp) output?
How do you keep duplicates out of a list?
questions.answer: Convert to a set and back: list(set(lst)) (order not guaranteed)

questions.question: How do you append multiple items with a loop?
What does [x for x in range(4)] produce?
How do you get the first 3 elements of a list?
How do you get the last 3 elements of a list?
What does [1, 2, 3, 4, 5][:3] return if you need the first half?
questions.answer: For the first half use slicing; lst[:3] gives [1, 2, 3] here

questions.question: How do you swap the first and last elements of a list?
What does lst.append(1) twice followed by lst do?
How do you find the second largest number in [3, 8, 5, 8]?
How do you find the index of the maximum value?
How do you split a string into a list of words?
How do you find the average of a list of numbers?
